name: Anger
description: Deal 6 damage. Place a copy of this card in your discard pile.
description_upgraded: Deal 8 damage. Place a copy of this card in your discard pile.
statement: An okay pick for act one, particularly when you are planning to fight the gremlin nob. Can help against enemies that pollute your deck, such as Hexaghost and the Sentries. In later acts, can cause you to have turns where you are unable to use all of your energy which is an ineffective use of your turn.

name: Armaments
description: Gain 5 Block. Upgrade a card in your hand for the rest of combat.
description_upgraded: Gain 5 Block. Upgrade ALL cards in your hand for the rest of combat.
statement: Armaments can be a very powerful card to upgrade first, as it likely has a lot of un-upgraded cards that it can hit throughout act 1. If Armaments makes any card that you wanted to play at least 1 energy cheaper, then it has already paid for itself. Even stronger if you can manage to couple it with some draw effects so it's hitting as many cards as possible. Can also be good in large decks where you don't have the opportunity to upgrade your whole deck.

name: Barricade
description: Block no longer expires at the start of your turn.
description_upgraded: Block no longer expires at the start of your turn.
statement: A very powerful win condition if you are able to draft big blocks with it, but due to its high cost it can fall flat in decks that don't support it. Entrench is a must-have pairing for longer fights.

name: Bash
description: Deal 8 damage. Apply 2 Vulnerable.
description_upgraded: Deal 10 damage. Apply 3 Vulnerable.
statement: Ironclad's bread and butter, Bash doesn't need to be removed from the deck as vulnerable works well with many of his strength synergies. Usually only consider upgrading if you don't have additional sources of vulnerable.

name: Battle Trance
description: Draw 3 cards. You cannot draw additional cards this turn.
description_upgraded: Draw 4 cards. You cannot draw additional cards this turn.
statement: Fantastic card, strong in many decks whether you have high energy or not. Be aware of its anti-draw effect. For this reason, drafting more than two battle trances in one deck can clutter your hand.

name: Berserk
description: Gain 2 vulnerable. At the start of your turn, gain 1 [energy].
description_upgraded: Gain 1 vulnerable. At the start of your turn, gain 1 [energy].
statement: Very powerful card, this is basically the equivalent of an energy relic in card form. Note that the vulnerability starts on this turn, meaning that unupgraded you are vulnerable this turn and next, and upgraded you are only vulnerable for this turn.

name: Blood for Blood
description: Costs 1 less [energy] for each time you lose HP in combat. Deal 18 damage.
description_upgraded: Costs 1 less [energy] for each time you lose HP in combat. Deal 22 damage.
statement: Too slow to be reliable, and generally speaking you do not want to be taking this much damage in fights. It acts as more of a consolation prize. Intentionally tanking one damage when blocking can improve the effectiveness of this card. For obvious reasons, intangible synergises very well.

name: Bloodletting
description: Lose 3 HP. Gain [energy] [energy].
description_upgraded: Lose 3 HP. Gain [energy] [energy] [energy].
statement: Strong as long as you have the cards draw to be able to make the most of all of the energy that you gain. Best when paired with some healing effects, as it is easy to slowly bleed out over the course of your run.

name: Bludgeon
description: Deal 32 damage.
description_upgraded: Deal 42 damage.
statement: A solid damage card early when it can one shot enemies. Its high cost can leave you open to counter attacks as you are usually unable to block on the same turn. Brilliant with damage amplifying effects.

name: Body Slam
description: Deal damage equal to your current Block.
description_upgraded: Deal damage equal to your current Block.
statement: Body Slam can be a game winning card and is a staple in the Barricade deck archetype. At 0 energy this becomes even more effective as it usually allows you to play one more block card before using it. Remember that this card’s damage is also increased by strength so even with 0 block it can do damage.

name: Brutality
description: At the start of your turn, lose 1 HP and draw 1 card.
description_upgraded: Innate. At the start of your turn, lose 1 HP and draw 1 card.
statement: Be wary of the amount of damage that you can accumulate when using Brutality. It is recommended that you take this card with some other form of healing. This card is exceptionally powerful with Rupture, as it also grants you one strength per turn. On some slow fights, playing this will not be worth it.

name: Burning Pact
description: Exhaust 1 card. Draw 2 cards.
description_upgraded: Exhaust 1 card. Draw 3 cards.
statement: Used to thin decks, only valuable once you have the energy to use this. Can be used to burn curses in certain scenarios, but remember the card must be exhausted before drawing takes place. If this is the last card in your hand, it doesn't exhaust anything.

name: Carnage
description: Ethereal. Deal 20 damage.
description_upgraded: Ethereal. Deal 28 damage.
statement: Carnage is a powerful card with very few downsides. I would definitely recommend this card early on in the run and later on it can do well as a solid source of damage if running a defensive deck. The ethereal nature of this card is almost completely irrelevant, as it is rarely a win condition and there are other ways of ending a fight.

name: Clash
description: Can only be played if every card in your hand is an Attack. Deal 14 damage.
description_upgraded: Can only be played if every card in your hand is an Attack. Deal 18 damage.
statement: Although this card is powerful on earlier ascensions, as soon as Ascender’s Bane starts appearing in the deck this card becomes extremely unreliable. In theory, clash can be played so long as you play out the other skills and powers in your hand, but in practice this is often clunky, not optimal, or too expensive, and curses and status cards are often impossible to play out.

name: Cleave
description: Deal 8 damage to ALL enemies.
description_upgraded: Deal 11 damage to ALL enemies.
statement: A solid AOE card but nothing special. I would recommend picking at least 1 multi target attack by the end of act 1.

name: Clothesline
description: Deal 12 damage. Apply 2 Weak.
description_upgraded: Deal 14 damage. Apply 3 Weak.
statement: A solid and consistent source of weak for ironclad that does not exhaust, making it a common pick in many decks. Less effective against enemies with artifact due to its high cost.

name: Combust
description: At the end of your turn, lose 1 HP and deal 5 damage to ALL enemies.
description_upgraded: At the end of your turn, lose 1 HP and deal 7 damage to ALL enemies.
statement: Generally this card is not as effective as it first seems, since its aoe effect is often to its detriment: typically, you want to kill enemies one by one in quick succession rather than slowly whittling them all down at the same time. it is easy for the health loss to stack up over time, particularly during longer encounters and boss fights. On the other hand, this is good versus enemies who apply the weak debuff or have other forms of attack damage mitigation, such as the byrds. This card is exceptionally powerful with Rupture, as it also grants you one strength per turn.

name: Corruption
description: Skills cost 0. Whenever you play a Skill, Exhaust it.
description_upgraded: Skills cost 0. Whenever you play a Skill, Exhaust it.
statement: This card is an exceptionally powerful win condition, but it is also a risky strategy. Corruption is powerful on the first time through your deck but once your deck is reshuffled and all of your defensive capabilities have been exhausted the fights can become scary. This is why it is very important to be careful how early you cast corruption, particularly in fights that you expect to be long such as boss battles. This card in combination with dead branch is one of the most insane combos in the entire game, as each skill that you exhaust has a chance of generating another free skill and so on and so forth. I typically recommend running one or two Iron Waves in this deck just in case a fight just go longer than you expect it to and you still need a source of block. Barricade can also work very well with corruption as the block that you accumulate does not expire right away. Dark Embrace can lead to cycling your first deck shuffle very quickly too, for better or for worse, and Feel No Pain amps up the block gain.

name: Dark Embrace
description: Whenever a card is Exhausted, draw 1 card.
description_upgraded: Whenever a card is Exhausted, draw 1 card.
statement: Dark embrace is usually only picked in conjunction with corruption. In theory it is possible to get value out of this power through cards that exhaust themselves or other cards but the payoff is rarely worth it.

name: Demon Form
description: At the start of each turn, gain 2 Strength.
description_upgraded: At the start of each turn, gain 3 Strength.
statement: Absolutely game winning in boss fights. Picking one is always a good idea, more than one is usually excessive. Goes great with Limit Break and Heavy Blade. Not always suitable for hallway fights.

name: Disarm
description: Enemy loses 2 Strength. Exhaust.
description_upgraded: Enemy loses 3 Strength. Exhaust.
statement: An exceptionally powerful defensive option in ironclad who doesn't usually have that many. Turns certain encounters into a joke, such as the plant, Hexaghost and the Heart to some extent. Picking one or two of these is never wrong.

name: Double Tap
description: This turn, your next Attack is played twice.
description_upgraded: This turn, your next 2 Attacks are played twice.
statement: Double tap is typically much more effective on expensive attacks, since the second time it is played it is played for free. Obvious choices are bludgeon, searing blow, and carnage. Cards that apply vulnerable benefit from the damage boost on the second play. This card can also get greater value out of Reaper. Also synergises with relics that work based on attacks played, such as Shuriken, Kunai, Pen Nib, etc.

name: Dropkick
description: Deal 5 damage. If the target is Vulnerable, gain [energy] and draw 1 card.
description_upgraded: Deal 8 damage. If the target is Vulnerable, gain [energy] and draw 1 card.
statement: A lot of the time, this card is worse than a strike - and even at its best, it's only 5 free damage. Can work if you have 3 or more ways of applying vulnerable, but otherwise often underperforms. Decks that build around this mechanic do exist with multiple copies of dropkick for fast free cycling, but this strategy struggles against the Time-Eater (12 turns), Deca and Donu (Artifacts) and the Heart (damage per card played).

name: Dual Wield
description: Create a copy of an Attack or Power card in your hand.
description_upgraded: Create 2 copies of an Attack or Power card in your hand.
statement: Dual wield typically works well with either cheap cards or by duplicating your wind conditions. For example, adding additional copies of a supercharged searing blow to your deck can make boss fights a breeze. Additionally, this card can be good with free attacks, as often if you are copying a card that costs more than 1 energy you wouldn't be able to play all of them in the same turn anyway. For this reason, it can work quite well with dropkick given that the enemy is already vulnerable. Of course, this card also works on powers, although some powers such as corruption do not benefit from being played again. Metallicize, fire breathing and rupture are some of the best power candidates. Note that any discounts on the original card apply to the copies as well.

name: Entrench
description: Double your current Block.
description_upgraded: Double your current Block.
statement: Entrench on its own is typically a terrible card. Very commonly you end up with no block options in hand and entrench therefore offers 0 block, and even when it does hit it typically provides 5 block for 2 energy – a terrible deal. This card DOES however have the potential to be insanely powerful when combined with barricade. I would never take this card unless I already had barricade or was working towards a barricade archetype.

name: Evolve
description: Whenever you draw a Status, draw 1 card.
description_upgraded: Whenever you draw a Status, draw 2 cards.
statement: Though niche, this card has the power to render certain battles laughable. The dazes from the Sentries elite and the Chosen's Hex debuff are nullified. It makes the downside of pollute cards (that add statuses to your deck) negligible. Even in fights where it does nothing, it can be simply played for 1 energy to exhaust it or in shorter fights it can simply be ignored.

name: Exhume
description: Choose an Exhausted card and put it in your hand. Exhaust.
description_upgraded: Choose an Exhausted card and put it in your hand. Exhaust.
statement: The power of exhume depends entirely on your exhaust cards. It can be powerful with Reaper to maximise healing or with feed to maximise HP gain, although finding the ideal scenario to pull this off is difficult. Note that you cannot exhume an exhume for infinite combos. Note that this can also bring back an important card that got exhausted by something like a Fiend Fire.

name: Feed
description: Deal 10 damage. If Fatal, raise your Max HP by 3. Exhaust.
description_upgraded: Deal 12 damage. If Fatal, raise your Max HP by 4. Exhaust.
statement: The earlier you take this card the better. Can be game-winning if you are able to stack it consistently. Consider stalling non-threatening hallway fights to get another Feed proc if you can do so without taking damage.

name: Feel No Pain
description: Whenever a card is Exhausted, gain 3 Block.
description_upgraded: Whenever a card is Exhausted, gain 4 Block.
statement: A card that synergises very well with corruption, but without it tends to fall flat. The extra occasional block from this effect can work in a deck that has a few standard exhausting cards, but this strategy rarely scales into the late game without huge sources of exhaust. Note that ethereal cards trigger this effect too.

name: Fiend Fire
description: Exhaust your hand. Deal 7 damage for each Exhausted card. Exhaust.
description_upgraded: Exhaust your hand. Deal 10 damage for each Exhausted card. Exhaust.
statement: A great source of fast damage. Ideal for corridor fights, but can leave you without important cards in longer elite or boss fights. Bonus points if your deck synergises with exhaust.

name: Fire Breathing
description: Whenever you draw a Status or Curse card, deal 6 damage to ALL enemies.
description_upgraded: Whenever you draw a Status or Curse card, deal 10 damage to ALL enemies.
statement: Running one copy of fire breathing is usually enough to hard counter certain fights without posing too much of a disadvantage in fights where it is useless. This power is also a build-around card and can be picked with cards that pollute your deck, such as second wind, wild strike, and reckless charge to make it powerful in any encounter. It also makes curses less of a drawback.

name: Flame Barrier
description: Gain 12 Block. Whenever you are attacked this turn, deal 4 damage to the attacker.
description_upgraded: Gain 16 Block. Whenever you are attacked this turn, deal 6 damage to the attacker.
statement: One of ironclads best block cards, flame barrier is a solid amount of block with the potential to deal moderate damage. A well-timed flame barrier can destroy the birds, is powerful versus the Hexaghost and in the right situation can deal up to 90 damage to the Heart in one turn.

name: Flex
description: Gain 2 Strength. At the end of your turn, lose 2 Strength.
description_upgraded: Gain 4 Strength. At the end of your turn, lose 4 Strength.
statement: Although flex seems to perform well in lower ascensions, it lacks the value required to compete at higher ascensions. If drawn without any attacks in hand, it is effectively useless. It must affect 3 attacks in order to be better than Anger, which is easier said than done in ironclad. What's more, the strength debuff that it applies can consume your artifact stacks, which is usually a bad thing although in some instances using it to permanently gain 4 strength can be powerful.

name: Ghostly Armor
description: Ethereal. Gain 10 Block.
description_upgraded: Ethereal. Gain 13 Block.
statement: This is a high-value, solid block card for ironclad and its ethereal nature is rarely relevant.

name: Havoc
description: Play the top card of your draw pile and Exhaust it.
description_upgraded: Play the top card of your draw pile and Exhaust it.
statement: Havoc is an extremely dangerous card. Although it has the potential to high roll and play expensive and powerful cards for zero energy, the fact that you do not get to pick the targets for the attack makes the card much worse. Furthermore, havoc exhausts the card, which means your win condition such as a supercharged searing blow could be exhausted. Other times, you might accidentally hit an enemy with thorns, accidentally reach a certain health threshold on a specific boss, or even accidentally exhaust your entire hand. Having a run end due to Havoc is extremely saddening. Cards such as warcry and headbutt allow you to choose which card havoc triggers, assuming you draw one of these cards alongside havoc and the card that you want is either in your discard pile or also in your hand (if this sounds unlikely to happen, it’s because it is). Note that X cost cards do not actually use any energy.

name: Headbutt
description: Deal 9 damage. Place a card from your discard pile on top of your draw pile.
description_upgraded: Deal 12 damage. Place a card from your discard pile on top of your draw pile.
statement: Best suited to bigger decks, as you have a larger pool of cards to choose from on average.

name: Heavy Blade
description: Deal 14 damage. Strength affects Heavy Blade 3 times.
description_upgraded: Deal 14 damage. Strength affects Heavy Blade 5 times.
statement: Heavy blade gets the highest value out of strength for any ironclad card except for pummel. pommels disadvantage however is that it exhausts. A very solid card in strength decks, but I would not recommend this card before finding any strength cards or relics as at 2 energy it underperforms.

name: Hemokinesis
description: Lose 2 HP. Deal 15 damage.
description_upgraded: Lose 2 HP. Deal 20 damage.
statement: Despite this card's high damage, it is very easy to slowly bleed out throughout the course of a run if you're not careful. In many scenarios, this card is able to kill an enemy before they attack, effectively reducing the amount of health you would lose overall. However it performs much worse against bosses with high health totals that require many attacks to kill. Obviously, this card synergises well with the likes of Rupture. Tungsten can also be useful in preventing damage.

name: Immolate
description: Deal 21 damage to ALL enemies. Shuffle a Burn into your discard pile.
description_upgraded: Deal 28 damage to ALL enemies. Shuffle a Burn into your discard pile.
statement: Immolate is a really powerful attack for hallway fights. It has very high aoe damage and is capable of killing multiple foes in one turn. the burn card goes into your discard pile so in many fights you are unlikely to even draw it before the encounter is over. This card is less effective versus single target enemies with high health totals and against bosses, as the burns will add up , deal damage to you and begin cluttering your hand. This card stops being as effective in act 3 but can carry runs if picked up early.

name: Impervious
description: Gain 30 Block. Exhaust.
description_upgraded: Gain 40 Block. Exhaust.
statement: Impervious is a powerful card, And I would normally pick it over skipping, but often there are better rare cards in ironclad. it can save a run from time to time if it is drawn on the right turn. Can be very useful versus the heart. This card is at its best in a barricade deck, as often the block is slightly overkill and barricade ensures that impervious always hits maximum value.

name: Infernal Blade
description: Add a random Attack to your hand. It costs 0 this turn. Exhaust.
description_upgraded: Add a random Attack to your hand. It costs 0 this turn. Exhaust.
statement: This is a card that I would only really consider taking on act one. it is very unreliable and later on in a run when you have higher energy you might find that you are ending the turn with energy to spare when you draw this card. The power of the card lies in its ability to create an expensive attack such as bludgeon and allow you to play it for free. The worst case scenarios for this card are hardly terrible, but its unpredictable nature makes it a liability and often times you would be better with a leaner deck.

name: Inflame
description: Gain 2 Strength.
description_upgraded: Gain 3 Strength.
statement: Inflame is a very solid power. It allows you to lean into a strength deck without fully committing (unlike limit break by contrast) and strength is relevant to every single ironclad deck (with the exception of Juggernaut, perhaps). It is cheap, easily played and good value.

name: Intimidate
description: Apply 1 Weak to ALL enemies. Exhaust.
description_upgraded: Apply 2 Weak to ALL enemies. Exhaust.
statement: Intimidate is a fine early pick, as it gives ironclad a defensive option that does not require any energy. However, the fact that it only applies 1 weak means that drawing it on a turn where the enemy is not attacking makes it a pointless draw, and since it exhausts it’s not reliable for longer fights. You will need an additional source of weak later on.

name: Iron Wave
description: Gain 5 Block. Deal 5 damage.
description_upgraded: Gain 7 Block. Deal 7 damage.
statement: Iron wave is decent early on, for example versus the Louse encounter. It is okay as a filler card as it is fairly high value but it's nothing special. Can be used in Corruption decks as a source of block once all your skills have been exhausted. This card uniquely benefits from both strength and dexterity and can slot into Kunai/Shuriken decks well.

name: Juggernaut
description: Whenever you gain Block, deal 5 damage to a random enemy.
description_upgraded: Whenever you gain Block, deal 7 damage to a random enemy.
statement: This card can serve as a builder round win condition in very specific decks, although it might struggle versus certain encounters. The hex debuff in particular is very difficult to work with in a deck with mostly skills. Is it worth mentioning that this card works very well with Metallicize and any form of plated armor. This power can be run in conjunction with a barricade deck although it is not strictly necessary. More often than not however, the fact that the damage is random can make it difficult to reliably finish targets off and the damage does not scale with vulnerable which can be too slow in many fights.

name: Limit Break
description: Double your Strength. Exhaust.
description_upgraded: Double your Strength.
statement: In the right decks, can lead to insane amounts of damage; however, without any strength cards to support it this card is as good as a curse. Doubling 1 strength isn't even enough justification to play this card. Never pick this without any form of strength gain.

name: Metallicize
description: At the end of your turn, gain 3 Block.
description_upgraded: At the end of your turn, gain 4 Block.
statement: This card is solid as it provides a lot of value over time, though it is nothing to write home about. It does not serve as a win condition, but it will likely prevent around 15 damage in a normal fight which is strong for its energy cost. Stacking Metallicize can be a strong strategy, meaning that your second and third copy of this card are actually more valuable than the first. The continuously stacking block works well with barricade, although it does not rely on it, and it also synergises well with plated armour. Generally pick it early or not at all.

name: Offering
description: Lose 6 HP. Gain [energy] [energy]. Draw 3 cards. Exhaust.
description_upgraded: Lose 6 HP. Gain [energy] [energy]. Draw 5 cards. Exhaust.
statement: Offering is a card with a very powerful effect but a pretty huge downside. Although it provides a lot of options through its additional draw and energy gain, it completely negates the healing that you get from your relic. As long as the effect is preventing you from taking six damage in the long room, for example by providing additional energy for block or by ensuring a monster is dead before it deals a high damaging attack, then you are using this card effectively. I would generally recommend having at least one additional source of healing to make this card worth the risk. It is possible to abstain from playing it uncertain fights that are low threat, but this usually feels terrible as ironclad doesn't typically have many options for drawing anyway.

name: Perfected Strike
description: Deal 6 damage. Deals an additional +2 damage for ALL of your cards containing "Strike".
description_upgraded: Deal 6 damage. Deals an additional +3 damage for ALL of your cards containing "Strike".
statement: I would only consider taking this card on the first half of act one. As a base, it is 18 damage for 2 energy which is about average value. This is okay early but must be built around in the later stages of the game to remain relevant, or else removed. Perfected strike decks often end up with around 40 cards in, meaning that your draw can become quite unreliable. If playing a perfected strike deck, you should take all other perfected strikes that are offered as well. Consider running Headbutts to pull it back as many times as possible. This strategy is inconsistent and I would not recommend it at high ascension.

name: Pommel Strike
description: Deal 9 damage. Draw 1 card.
description_upgraded: Deal 10 damage. Draw 2 cards.
statement: Pommel strike is a filler card which I would pick in situations where I am lacking draw after having gained at least one form of energy relic. Until you have extra energy, the draw is usually pointless.

name: Power Through
description: Add 2 Wounds to your hand. Gain 15 Block.
description_upgraded: Add 2 Wounds to your hand. Gain 20 Block.
statement: Power through exists as a defensive option that synergises with pollute decks. For this reason it synergises decently well with Fire Breathing. I typically would not pick this card without any pollute synergies, since the two wounds can quickly clutter a deck. Evolve can be used to offset the pollute effect but be aware that it is possible to have a hand with 10 cards in, most of which are wounds. as a caveat, since the wounds are directly added to your hand they can be used with Fiend Fire or Second Wind as additional fuel.

name: Pummel
description: Deal 2 damage 4 times. Exhaust.
description_upgraded: Deal 2 damage 5 times. Exhaust.
statement: Great for dealing with byrds at the start of Act 2. Most commonly sees play in a strength deck. Since this card exhausts, it cannot be considered a reliable win condition for longer fights in decks that are built around stacking strength.

name: Rage
description: Whenever you play an Attack this turn, gain 3 Block.
description_upgraded: Whenever you play an Attack this turn, gain 5 Block.
statement: Rage, like flex, is a fairly inconsistent card. On its own, it does nothing, and in a typical hand it may only provide 9 block. I would definitely not recommend this card at high ascensions, but if you are on a low ascension and you find that you have a very aggressive deck with not many sources of block then this can act as a band-aid and save you.

name: Rampage
description: Deal 8 damage. Every time this card is played, increase its damage by 5 for this combat.
description_upgraded: Deal 8 damage. Every time this card is played, increase its damage by 8 for this combat.
statement: Can be a win condition if the deck focuses on replaying this card repeatedly, but this strategy is inconsistent at higher ascension. Best in slim decks or decks that exhaust. Can be a useful tool against Hexaghost for example if your deck is low on dps.

name: Reaper
description: Deal 4 damage to ALL enemies. Heal for unblocked damage. Exhaust.
description_upgraded: Deal 5 damage to ALL enemies. Heal for unblocked damage. Exhaust.
statement: Reaper is an incredibly powerful card, and possibly one of ironclad’s strongest. Without any support, the healing that it does is fairly negligible, however its damage and healing is increased by vulnerable and as soon as you start stacking strength this card becomes incredibly strong. It's possible to heal upwards of 50 health in one combat in the right situation. It is not always correct to play repair on the turn that you draw it - sometimes you want to wait for more procs of Demon Form or your Limit Break. Keep in mind that Reaper can only heal for damage done - overkill does not heal you for the excess amount.

name: Reckless Charge
description: Deal 7 damage. Shuffle a Dazed into your draw pile.
description_upgraded: Deal 10 damage. Shuffle a Dazed into your draw pile.
statement: Reckless Charge can be a good pick in act 1 when 0 energy cards are more valuable, and also when the dazed effect does not typically stop you from using all of your energy every turn. This card’s downside can be used to its advantage when running a pollute deck with powers like Fire Breathing and Evolve. Don't forget that the ethereal dazed card will also exhaust itself at the end of the turn, which can trigger exhaust bonuses from relics like Charon’s Ashes.

name: Rupture
description: Whenever you lose HP from a card, gain 1 Strength.
description_upgraded: Whenever you lose HP from a card, gain 2 Strength.
statement: Rupture is a slow but steady source of strength when combined with powers such as combust and brutality. It also works with curse damage (to great effect with Pain) and burn damage. I would never pick this card without having a single source of self damage already, and ideally you have two or three. The main benefit to this card is that it is inexpensive 1 compared to something like demon form; however demon form is much more reliable, consistent and does not require support from other cards. Be aware that Tungsten Rod can prevent all damage from Combust and Brutality, preventing strength gain.

name: Searing Blow
description: Deal 12 damage. Can be upgraded any number of times.
description_upgraded: Deal 16 damage. Can be upgraded any number of times.
statement: Can be a winning card if the deck focuses on upgrading this card almost exclusively. Each upgrade provides a bigger bonus than the last. Should be played in small decks to get as many plays as possible. Be aware that almost every single upgrade will be dedicated to this card, so don't pick cards that are only valuable when upgraded (such as True Grit).

name: Second Wind
description: Exhaust all non-Attack cards in your hand and gain 5 Block for each.
description_upgraded: Exhaust all non-Attack cards in your hand and gain 7 Block for each.
statement: This card can be difficult to use as it can put you in situations where you have to choose between taking damage and exhausting key cards (such as a Demon Form). Remember that you can play cards that you don't want to be exhausted, as long as you have the energy and don't need the additional block. This card can work well in a pollute deck with the likes of Power Through as it is very effective at removing wounds and burns from your deck, although this strategy can be fairly unreliable without strong draw cards. Needless to say, this card pairs very well with Dead Branch, like all other exhaust strategies, and fits very well into exhaust-focused decks that run powers like Feel No Pain and Dark Embrace.

name: Seeing Red
description: Gain [energy] [energy]. Exhaust.
description_upgraded: Gain [energy] [energy]. Exhaust.
statement: A solid energy card which is rare for ironclad. Ironclad has very expensive attacks when compared to other classes so it is not normally difficult to get full value out of this card. The more sources of energy you have, the less powerful this card becomes, which makes it a strong early pick but its effectiveness tends to drop off without strong sources of draw. Pairs well with Ice Cream for obvious reasons.

name: Sentinel
description: Gain 5 Block. If this card is Exhausted, gain [energy] [energy].
description_upgraded: Gain 8 Block. If this card is Exhausted, gain [energy] [energy] [energy].
statement: Only ever pick this if you have Corruption.

name: Sever Soul
description: Exhaust all non-Attack cards in your hand. Deal 16 damage.
description_upgraded: Exhaust all non-Attack cards in your hand. Deal 20 damage.
statement: Sever Soul is a strong source of damage for its energy cost with few downsides. Be careful not to exhaust key cards in your deck, for example a Demon Form, although playing these cards before Sever Soul saves them from being exhausted so long as you have the energy. This card can work well in a pollute deck with the likes of Power Through as it is very effective at removing wounds and burns from your deck, although this strategy can be fairly unreliable without strong draw cards. Needless to say, this card pairs very well with Dead Branch, like all other exhaust strategies, and fits very well into exhaust-focused decks that run powers like Feel No Pain and Dark Embrace.

name: Shockwave
description: Apply 3 Weak and Vulnerable to ALL enemies. Exhaust
description_upgraded: Apply 5 Weak and Vulnerable to ALL enemies. Exhaust
statement: Although expensive, the shockwave played early in combat can debuff enemies long enough to ensure most are dead by the end of its duration, and to mitigate damage until then. A decent card, and a good substitute for Uppercut and Clothesline where necessary. Can be hard to play this card with just 3 energy, so energy gain is recommended.

name: Shrug It Off
description: Gain 8 Block. Draw 1 card.
description_upgraded: Gain 11 Block. Draw 1 card.
statement: Although Shrug It Off is a common card, it is extremely reliable, offering a decent source of block and draw in a class that doesn't have much of either, making it very valuable. It is a typical to finish a run with three copies of this card.

name: Spot Weakness
description: If an enemy intends to attack, gain 3 Strength.
description_upgraded: If an enemy intends to attack, gain 4 Strength.
statement: Spot weakness is a decent source of instant strength and its conditions are easily met. The benefit of spot weakness is that it can be played multiple times in a single fight, unlike Inflame. Demon forms strength gain is more consistent, but also slower and more expensive, making spot weakness more effective in hallway fights. In practice, if you are running a strength deck, you will likely be running a combination of all of these cards.

name: Sword Boomerang
description: Deal 3 damage to a random enemy 3 times.
description_upgraded: Deal 3 damage to a random enemy 4 times.
statement: Sword Boomerang is only to be picked in strength decks. Be aware that you do not choose Sword Boomerang’s targets which can make this very unreliable and frustrating. This card becomes supercharged with enough strength, so much so that you can finish off hordes of enemies with a single use, offsetting its randomness. A fair substitute for Heavy Blade, though usually slightly worse.

name: Thunderclap
description: Deal 4 damage and apply 1 Vulnerable to ALL enemies.
description_upgraded: Deal 7 damage and apply 1 Vulnerable to ALL enemies.
statement: Thunderclap is a fairly unremarkable card due to the fact that it only applies 1 vulnerable. It has unimpressive damage and is only powerful when paired with another aoe card on the same turn, which can be hard to execute. Be aware that Thunderclap can work with cards like bash by extending the duration of vulnerable without requiring damage on the same turn. Strength can also greatly increase the effectiveness of this card.

name: True Grit
description: Gain 7 Block. Exhaust a random card from your hand.
description_upgraded: Gain 9 Block. Exhaust a card from your hand.
statement: True Grit is another strong source of block for the ironclad, and the selective exhaust ability is not to be underestimated. It can be used to remove curses or status cards from your hand, or even remove niche cards that are not relevant to this encounter (such as an Evolve) or just generally low value (Strikes and Defends). Note that this card must be upgraded for you to be able to choose which card is exhausted, and as such it is highly recommended that this card is upgraded if selected. Slight exhaust synergy.

name: Twin Strike
description: Deal 5 damage twice.
description_upgraded: Deal 7 damage twice.
statement: Twin strike is an okay card which can provide some DPS in the early game whilst also being able to lean into the strength archetype without committing to it. It is an important card against the byrds and I recommend picking up at least one source of multihit in act 1, whether or not you're running a strength deck.

name: Uppercut
description: Deal 13 damage. Apply 1 Weak. Apply 1 Vulnerable.
description_upgraded: Deal 13 damage. Apply 2 Weak. Apply 2 Vulnerable.
statement: Uppercut is a potent debuff card which can be effective against single target encounters. It is difficult to make use of the vulnerable proc on the same turn, and it is therefore recommended that you upgrade this card. Uppercut is a good substitute for Clothesline.

name: Warcry
description: Draw a card. Place a card from your hand on top of your draw pile. Exhaust.
description_upgraded: Draw 2 cards. Place a card from your hand on top of your draw pile. Exhaust.
statement: This card is intended to be used to make your current turn and the next turn have better options. It synergises well with Havoc, since you can control which card is played and exhausted. You might think that this card has no possible downsides since it is free and draws, but enemies like the Chosen, the Time-Eater and the Heart make Warcry a less valuable pick. For this reason, I would not generally recommend picking one except perhaps early. As a side-note, warcry can be used in combination with Fire Breathing to draw and re-shuffle curses and statuses into your deck.

name: Whirlwind
description: Deal 5 damage to ALL enemies X times.
description_upgraded: Deal 8 damage to ALL enemies X times.
statement: Whirlwind is a decent and reliable card as it allows you to spend all of your energy on the turn that you draw it (except against a spiker perhaps). It also scales incredibly well with strength. Since it is X cost, it can be played with 0 energy to proc certain relics, such as Kunai and Shuriken. Overall a very reliable card with potential upsides.

name: Wild Strike
description: Deal 12 damage. Shuffle a Wound into your draw pile.
description_upgraded: Deal 17 damage. Shuffle a Wound into your draw pile.
statement: Without any pollute synergies, I would consider taking wild strike perhaps on act 1, where even on turns where you draw a wound you are still able to spend all of your energy. It is a lot of fast damage making it useful in corridor fights, although the wounds can stack up if you have no way of dealing with them. This is why it's best to take wild strike in a deck that to make the most of pollution, such as one with Fire Breathing and Evolve.
